comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company recorded an income tax provision of $381 million and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2024 and 2023, with effective tax rates of 19% and (68%) respectively, driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD attribute changes in their income tax provisions to specific non-recurring or structural intercompany events in fiscal 2024. AVGO cites a 'non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights' resulting from supply chain realignment, while AMD cites a '$373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.' Additionally, both companies note that higher pre-tax income was a driver for the increase in tax provision, though AVGO's increase was further impacted by jurisdictional shifts, whereas AMD's effective tax rate was heavily influenced by prior year benefits (2023 benefit vs 2024 provision).

sentences.text: The increase in provision for income taxes in fiscal year 2024 compared to fiscal year 2023 was primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States as a result of supply chain realignment and the resulting shift in jurisdictional mix of income, partially offset by an increase in excess tax benefits from stock-based awards.
The Company recorded an income tax provision of $381 million and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2024 and 2023, respectively, representing effective tax rates of 19% and (68)%, respectively.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

comparisons.peer_topic: Recognition and amounts of income tax benefits for share-based awards
comparisons.peer_summary: Income tax benefits related to tax deductions for share-based awards are recognized upon settlement of the awards, amounting to $140 million, $68 million, and $77 million for the fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose the impact of stock-based awards on their income tax provisions. AVGO notes that its increase in tax provision was 'partially offset by an increase in excess tax benefits from stock-based awards,' indicating a reduction in the effective tax rate due to these awards. MU provides specific quantitative data on this same line item, stating that 'Income tax benefits for share-based awards were $140 million' in fiscal 2024, which represents a cash tax benefit recognized upon settlement. Both disclosures highlight this specific driver within the broader income tax provision discussion.

sentences.text: The increase in provision for income taxes in fiscal year 2024 compared to fiscal year 2023 was primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States as a result of supply chain realignment and the resulting shift in jurisdictional mix of income, partially offset by an increase in excess tax benefits from stock-based awards.
Income tax benefits for share-based awards were $140 million, $68 million, and $77 million for 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
